title: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd - 500008 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 15-16% to INR3,530 crore, with lead-acid margin near 12% despite raw-material inflation.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR3,530 crore, up close to 15% YoY, with about 92% from Lead Acid Batteries and about INR280 crore from New Energy. Lead-acid revenue grew about 12% and 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler OEM volumes grew more than 30%, while aftermarket grew 5-6%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 11%, and lead-acid operating margin was about 11.6% after adjusting for lithium pack trading, with management citing raw-material and alloy cost spikes linked to the geopolitical conflict. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR13,814 crore (up about 7.5%) with a 10.8% consolidated margin; the company guided FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore, mostly in New Energy.

financial_highlights.change: up close to 15% YoY (16% per management later)

financial_highlights.metric: Lead Acid Battery revenue growth Q4 FY26
Lead Acid operating margin Q4 FY26 (ex lithium trading)

segments.name: Lead Acid Battery (Automotive and Industrial)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 12% YoY in Q4; 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler OEM volumes up more than 30%, aftermarket up 5-6%, other industrial segments up 3-4%, telecom lead-acid declining as it shifts to lithium. Price hikes of 5-6% taken in domestic automotive in Q4 in tranches.

segments.name: Tubular batteries and Home UPS
segments.commentary: Tubular battery volumes grew more than 35% in Q4; in-house share is 70-75% with 20-25% now traded from other manufacturers. Home energy demand described as sustained.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Lubes business has reached a run-rate of about INR50 crore revenue per quarter.

segments.name: New Energy (Lithium packs, chargers, BESS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR280 crore; more than 300 MWh of telecom packs supplied in the quarter and about 1 GWh of telecom packs supplied in FY26. INR100 crore infused into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies in Q4, taking total investment to about INR1,500 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 industry growth expected mid to high single digit; company aims to grow ahead of market, with high single-digit growth guided for FY27 as management indicated.
Management is still aiming for a 13-14% EBITDA margin on a standalone basis over time, despite lead prices around INR210,000-220,000 per tonne, but gave no timeline.
Another 2-3% price increase expected, with the company saying this may not fully recover cost pressure; no price hike taken yet in the current quarter.
FY27 capex planned at INR1,500-1,700 crore: about INR400 crore for Lead Acid and INR1,100-1,200 crore for New Energy.
BESS integration facility at Divitipally targeted to start production at end of calendar 2026 with 5 GWh initial capacity, expandable to 10 GWh; BESS operating margin initially 6-7%.
Giga 1 (2 GWh cell line, 2170 cylindrical) expected to start production in June 2027; LFP products expected 2028 or later; 16 GWh Divitipally target unchanged.
Targeted 8-10 GWh scale for cell business with EBITDA margin of 10-11% and ROCE expected to be low double-digit, per management business case.
capex_capacity: Lead Acid capex about INR600 crore in FY26 gross (about INR500 crore net of insurance claim), across battery and recycling businesses; rest spent on New Energy, including R&D lab and Customer Qualification Plant (CQP).
CQP in final commissioning; commercial samples expected to customers in the next couple of months; full-scale operations expected in coming months.
E Positive Energy Labs R&D centre in final commissioning, with teams moving in over the next month.
Equipment for 2 GWh (2170) Giga 1 line has been ordered; commissioning has been slowed by limited visas for Chinese engineers.
Capex cost estimate per GWh was $55-60 million when project started; management says it has fallen 20-25% since.
demand_pricing: Telecom lead-acid volumes declining as telecom shifts to lithium, but company retains about 50% share in telecom segment.
Exports muted in Q4 due to geopolitical conflict, tariffs in North America and shipping headwinds; exports about 12% of FY26 revenue, marginally lower YoY.
Raw materials: about 70% of lead acid RM basket is lead and alloys (tin, antimony); plastics about 10% and could rise about 40%; sulfur is pushing acid prices up; RML prices have risen sharply.
Raw-material and freight cost increases, plus higher OEM mix (lower margin), pressured Q4 margins; EPR and warranty costs are rising.
Captive recycling contributed about 0.5% margin benefit in the quarter, with battery-breaking expected to stabilise next quarter.
Price increases of 5-6% taken in domestic automotive in Q4; further 2-3% increase being considered depending on competitor moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is equipment for the 2 GWh cell line ordered, and what are the commissioning constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment has been ordered; the constraint is limited visas for Chinese engineers to commission it, with a few visas issued and engineers on ground at CQP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gotion partnership and LFP plant timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology licensing from China is being discouraged by Beijing; management says product development is now largely India-driven. The Gotion tie-up was corporate-to-corporate with no government approval sought. First capacity next year will be NMC; LFP is 2028 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS margins once stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial operating margin about 6-7%, with upside as scale improves; the BESS plant is seen as a strategic lever for ESS cell manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 outlook for replacement and industrial segments, and Q4 growth by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM 2W and 4W grew more than 30%, aftermarket 5-6%, other industrial 3-4%, telecom declining; FY27 growth guided at mid to high single digit.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation and price hikes should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead and alloys about 70% of RM; plastics about 10% with possible 40% increase; another 2-3% price increase likely, possibly insufficient to offset full cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Who is the offtaker for the 16 GWh capacity, and what is the ROCE on the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No binding offtake for the 2 GWh; EV programs have take-or-pay style safeguards; ESS to be offtaken partly by own systems. At 8-10 GWh scale, EBITDA margin 10-11% and ROCE expected low double-digit; cost disadvantage vs China imports of about 15-20% expected to be bridged over time with localisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will lead-acid capacity be underutilised as EV penetration rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a long runway for lead-acid given ICE OE growth, replacement demand and auxiliary batteries; telecom plant still running at 30-40 million Ah; capacity unlocked within existing footprint.

risks_watch: Lead and alloy prices (around INR210,000-220,000 per tonne), sulfur and freight costs keep pressuring margins; management says price hikes may not fully recover costs.
Rupee depreciation and dollar-linked alloy costs; daily forex volatility makes cost quantification uncertain.
Chinese engineer visa constraints and equipment vendor dependence could delay commissioning of CQP and Giga 1 (June 2027).
Chinese restrictions on technology licensing affect the Gotion tie-up and future LFP timing (2028 or later).
Lack of binding offtake for the planned 16 GWh cell capacity; reliance on own ESS demand and on localisation mandates that are not yet notified.
Export softness from geopolitics, tariffs and shipping; telecom lead-acid decline as lithium transition continues.
Recycling benefit (about 0.5%) depends on battery-breaking stabilisation and RML price moves.
Possible policy changes on localisation (ALMM-style) that could raise BESS costs for customers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core lead-acid franchise and OEM growth, but cautious on margins, input costs and the timing of the New Energy ramp-up. Management was openly hedged on pricing ("it's difficult for me to say" on the margin timeline) and on cost competitiveness versus Chinese imports.
key_quotes: At the moment, we also have our own challenges in terms of working directly in the sort of technology licensing or any sort of direct tie-ups with Chinese.
I'm happy to share that we have substantial updates for you.
We're aiming to start production at the end of this calendar year with an initial capacity of 5 gigawatt hour in a facility with the ultimate capacity of 10 gigawatt hour.
So I feel still 13% margin trajectory is something that is still on the horizon.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 growth at mid to high single digit (about 8% midpoint), aiming to grow ahead of industry; backing is partial, citing 4W/2W OEM volumes up 30%+, 5-6% price hikes, and a 2-3% further hike, with new capacity (BESS 5 GWh, Giga 1 2 GWh) mostly not live until FY28 or later.
